title: Continuity
body:
A function is **continuous at $a$** when three things hold at once:

1. $f(a)$ is defined
2. $\lim_{x \to a} f(x)$ exists
3. they are equal: $\lim_{x \to a} f(x) = f(a)$

Informally, you can draw it through that point without lifting the pen. The three conditions
matter because they fail separately, and which one fails names the discontinuity:

| Failure | Name | Picture |
|---|---|---|
| limit exists, $f(a)$ does not (or differs) | **removable** | a hole, patchable by redefining one point |
| one-sided limits exist but disagree | **jump** | a step |
| a one-sided limit is infinite | **infinite** | a vertical asymptote |

Continuous **on an interval** means continuous at every point of it, with one-sided continuity at
the endpoints of a closed interval. Polynomials are continuous everywhere; rational functions
everywhere except zeros of the denominator; $\sin$ and $\cos$ everywhere; $\ln$ on $(0,\infty)$.
Sums, products, quotients, and compositions of continuous functions are continuous, which is why
"just plug in" works for almost everything you meet.

## Continuity versus differentiability

> **[[Derivative|Differentiable]] $\Rightarrow$ continuous. The converse is false.**

$f(x) = |x|$ at $x = 0$ is the counterexample to keep: no hole, no jump, perfectly continuous, but
the left slope is $-1$ and the right slope is $+1$ so the difference quotient has no [[Limit]]. A
corner is continuous and not differentiable. So is a cusp, and so is a vertical tangent.

## Intermediate Value Theorem

> If $f$ is continuous on $[a,b]$ and $N$ is any value between $f(a)$ and $f(b)$, then $f(c) = N$
> for some $c$ in $(a,b)$.

The first **existence theorem** in the degree: it proves a solution is there without producing it.
The standard use is root-finding. If $f$ is continuous and $f(1) < 0 < f(2)$, then $f$ has a root
somewhere in $(1,2)$, guaranteed, and you have no idea where.

That guarantee is exactly what binary search on a continuous function (bisection) runs on: halve
the interval, keep the half where the sign still changes, repeat. Continuity is the hypothesis
that makes the "keep the half with the sign change" step valid. The discrete cousin,
[[Modified Binary Search|binary search on a sorted array]], gets the same guarantee from
sortedness instead. Drop the hypothesis in either case and the search can miss.

## Not to be confused with

[[Continuous]] in [[COMPUTING MACHINERY 2]] is signal vocabulary: a quantity with a value at every
instant and infinitely many values between any two, the opposite of [[Discrete]]. This note is the
analytic property of a *function* at a *point*. The two are related in spirit (both are about
having no gaps) and are not the same claim: a continuous-valued signal can perfectly well be a
discontinuous function of time.

## Related

- [[Limit]]: continuity is the statement that the limit equals the value
- [[Mean Value Theorem]] and [[Optimization]]: both need continuity as a hypothesis, and the
  Extreme Value Theorem needs a closed interval as well
